title: Top 10 Festivals in Seoul and Nearby This October (2026)
html:
Planning a trip to Korea in October? You've picked a great month — this is when Seoul, Incheon, and the surrounding Gyeonggi Province host some of their biggest annual festivals. All ten below are in the greater capital area, so you can reach every one of them by subway, train, or bus without needing a car. They're listed with Seoul first, then the nearby cities.

A quick tip before you go: almost all of these festivals are free to walk around and watch, but food stalls, workshops, and some ticketed shows cost extra. It's smart to bring a little cash or a Korean transit/payment card. Locals usually avoid Saturday and Sunday afternoons, when these events get most crowded — if you can, try a weekday evening or the first hour after opening instead.

1. Gangnam Festival (강남페스티벌)

This is one of Seoul's biggest city festivals, taking over the streets of Gangnam-gu for three days. Expect a big opening street parade, K-pop concerts, a "Fashion & Beauty Festa," and a "Beer & Food Festa" with food trucks. It's centered on Dosandaero Avenue, which runs between Sinsa Station and Apgujeong Rodeo Station (Seoul Subway Line 3/Bundang Line) — both easy to reach if you're staying in central Seoul.

  • Dates: October 3–5, 2026
  • Hours: 11:00–22:00
  • Admission: Free
  • Where: Dosandaero Avenue, Gaepo-dong Maru Park, and Bongeunsa Temple, Gangnam-gu, Seoul

2. Geumcheon Siheung Haenggung Cultural Festival (금천시흥행궁문화제)

A haenggung is a temporary palace that Korea's kings used to stay in while traveling outside the main royal palace — and Geumcheon-gu once had one. This one-day festival brings that history to life with historical reenactments and performances along the neighborhood's pretty ginkgo tree–lined road, a nice detour if fall foliage is on your list.

  • Dates: October 4, 2026 (one day only)
  • Hours: 12:00–20:00
  • Admission: Free
  • Where: Ginkgo Tree Road area, Geumcheon-gu, Seoul

3. Gangdong Prehistoric Culture Festival (강동선사문화축제)

Seoul's only festival dedicated to prehistoric culture, held at the real Amsa-dong Prehistoric Settlement Site — a Stone Age village discovered here decades ago. This is the 31st edition, with the festival grounds split into four themed zones and evening highlights including a drone show and a closing fireworks show. It's a fun, hands-on stop if you're traveling with kids.

  • Dates: October 16–18, 2026
  • Hours: Daytime through evening (night programs included)
  • Admission: Free
  • Where: Amsa-dong Prehistoric Settlement Site, Gangdong-gu, Seoul

4. Geumcheon Harmony Festival (금천하모니축제)

Geumcheon-gu's long-running neighborhood festival, held every year since 2003 and built around music. Come for a citizen choir performance, live music, a flea market, and food trucks in a relaxed park setting — a good pick if you want a slower, community-feel event rather than a huge crowd.

  • Dates: October 17–18, 2026
  • Hours: 11:00–20:00
  • Admission: Free
  • Where: Geumnarae Jungang Park and the Geumcheon-gu Office Plaza, Seoul

5. Goyang Autumn Flower Festival (고양가을꽃축제)

Held around Ilsan Lake Park in Goyang, just north of Seoul, this festival fills the park with chrysanthemums, cosmos, sunflowers, and zinnias in full bloom, plus flower art displays indoors. It's an easy, photogenic half-day trip if you want a break from the city.

  • Dates: October 1–11, 2026
  • Hours: 09:00–18:00
  • Admission: Free
  • Where: Ilsan Lake Park, Ilsandong-gu, Goyang-si, Gyeonggi-do

6. Anseong Namsadang Baudeogi Festival (안성맞춤 남사당 바우덕이축제)

This festival celebrates Namsadang Nori, a traditional Korean traveling performance art — tightrope walking, acrobatics, and mask dance — recognized by UNESCO as part of the world's intangible cultural heritage. It's named after Baudeogi, a famous 19th-century female troupe leader from this area. You'll also find a recreated old-style market street with food and craft stalls.

  • Dates: October 2–5, 2026
  • Hours: 10:00–21:00
  • Admission: Free
  • Where: Anseong Matchum Land and the Anseongcheon Stream area, Anseong-si, Gyeonggi-do

7. Bupyeong Pungmul Festival (부평풍물대축제)

Now in its 30th year, this festival fills the streets of Bupyeong with pungmul — traditional Korean farmers' music played on drums, gongs, and a small hand-held gong called a kkwaenggwari, often performed while dancing in a circle. Neighborhood drum troupes from all over the district take part in a lively parade. Bupyeong Station is a major transit hub (Seoul Subway Line 1, Incheon Subway Line 1, and Line 7), so it's simple to reach from Seoul.

  • Dates: October 2–4, 2026
  • Hours: 10:00–21:30
  • Admission: Free
  • Where: Bupyeong-daero and the surrounding Bupyeong area, Incheon

8. Soraepogu Festival (소래포구 축제)

Sorae Port is one of the last traditional fishing harbors near Seoul, well known for its seafood market. This festival celebrates the port's history and ecology with hands-on nature programs, resident-run stalls, cultural performances, and a fireworks show at night. Combine it with a seafood meal at the nearby market for a full day out.

  • Dates: October 2–4, 2026
  • Hours: 09:00–21:00
  • Admission: Free (some activities cost extra)
  • Where: Haeoreum Square and the Sorae Port area, Namdong-gu, Incheon

9. Suwon Hwaseong Festival (수원화성문화제)

Held at Suwon Hwaseong Fortress, a UNESCO World Heritage stone fortress about 40 minutes south of Seoul by train, this is one of Korea's largest historical festivals. Its centerpiece is a reenactment of King Jeongjo's 1795 royal procession — Korea's largest royal parade reenactment — along with themed night performances and a water show. It's a great pick if "K-drama historical palace" scenery is what you're after.

  • Dates: October 4–11, 2026
  • Hours: 12:00–21:00
  • Admission: Free (fees vary for some ticketed programs)
  • Where: Suwon Hwaseong Fortress, Paldal-gu, Suwon-si, Gyeonggi-do

10. Yeoju Ogoknaru Festival (여주오곡나루축제)

This is the farthest festival on the list — about 1.5–2 hours from Seoul by intercity bus — but worth the trip if you want a taste of rural Korea. "Ogok" means "five grains," and the festival celebrates Yeoju's rice-farming history, from the days when local rice and sweet potatoes were shipped down the river as royal tribute. Try the cast-iron-pot rice bibimbap, browse the local produce market, and stay for nakhwanori — a traditional fire show — after dark.

  • Dates: October 23–25, 2026
  • Hours: 10:00–21:00
  • Admission: Free
  • Where: Silleuksa Temple Resort, Yeoju-si, Gyeonggi-do

💬 Not sure which ones fit your itinerary, or have a question about getting to any of these? Drop it in the comments below — happy to help!
meta_description: From a UNESCO royal parade in Suwon to a folk drum festival in Incheon, here are the 10 biggest festivals happening in Seoul and nearby this October 2026.
